title: After the Raft
dek: Olympic runner, World War II airman, survivor, and public witness to endurance after the Pacific nearly erased him.
mortality_event: Survived a 1943 Pacific crash, 47 days adrift, and nearly two years as a Japanese prisoner of war before his later public testimony and forgiveness work.
sources: U.S. Air Force Veterans in Blue

sources.name: DOD News historical feature — Olympic Runner Louis Zamperini

closing_line: The reprieve was one moment. The work was the rest of his life.
citation_passage: Louis Zamperini (1917–2014) was an American Olympic runner and wartime airman whose survival extended from a Pacific crash to imprisonment. He competed in the 1936 Berlin Olympics before joining the Army Air Corps. When his B-24 crashed in 1943, he survived 47 days at sea before Japanese forces captured him. He endured prisoner-of-war camps and returned home after the war. His later account described a religious conversion and efforts to forgive former captors. This eight-page biographical comic follows the crash, raft, captivity, and life afterward, treating survival as a continuing story rather than an ending at rescue.
